identity.title: BIRD-INTERACT: Re-imagining Text-to-SQL Evaluation via Lens of Dynamic Interactions

problem.claim: Evaluate text-to-SQL models in realistic multi-turn database interactions involving ambiguity, execution errors, and changing requirements.

gap.claim: Existing multi-turn benchmarks either treat conversation history as static context or restrict evaluation to read-only SELECT operations, missing aspects of production database assistance.

contributions.claim: Introduces BIRD-INTERACT, an interaction environment combining databases with hierarchical knowledge bases, metadata, and a function-driven user simulator for clarification, knowledge retrieval, and error recovery.
Defines c-Interact with a prescribed conversational protocol and a-Interact, where models autonomously choose whether to query the simulator or explore the database environment.
Provides executable-test-guarded CRUD tasks spanning business-intelligence and operational use cases, in full and lite sets of 600 and 300 tasks respectively.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present BIRD-INTERACT as restoring realism to text-to-SQL evaluation through dynamic interaction, broader database operations, and an environment supporting autonomous interaction.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that GPT-5 completes 8.67% of full-suite tasks in c-Interact and 17.00% in a-Interact.
The authors report that memory grafting and Interaction Test-time Scaling analyses validate the importance of effective interaction for success on dynamic text-to-SQL tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Single-turn text-to-SQL performance does not address the multi-turn ambiguity, errors, and evolving requirements of real database applications.
Prior multi-turn benchmarks are described as static-context or SELECT-only evaluations that omit production-relevant complexity.
BIRD-INTERACT adds an interactive environment, protocol-driven and agentic settings, and CRUD tasks with executable tests.
The benchmark offers a 600-task full set with up to 11,796 dynamic interactions and a 300-task lite set for behavioral analysis and faster method development.
The authors report low GPT-5 completion rates and analyses emphasizing effective interaction.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs benchmark capabilities with explicit evaluation settings and reports separate completion rates for each setting.

lessons.interpretation: Separating interaction protocols can expose how performance changes with the model’s control over interaction.
lessons.application: When introducing an interactive benchmark, define fixed-protocol and autonomous variants and report results separately.
lessons.exception: This split may be unsuitable when the target deployment has only one fixed interaction policy.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify how tasks, executable tests, interaction success, or the reported analyses are implemented and measured.
The reported GPT-5 rates are given without baselines, uncertainty estimates, or comparisons to other models.
